newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Property jitters bruise Singapore stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: Property jitters bruise Singapore stocks at close.

text.p: Fears of more property curbs rattled Singapores stocks on Tuesday but the Ministry of National Development's denial that it plans to hold a news briefing this week gave the market a mild lift before the close.
Dealers said the market was rife with talk that the government is planning more curbs for the property market.

The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 6.59 points down at 1,990.20 after hitting a new year low of 1,981.92. The SES property index ended 10.08 points off at 646.96 after sinking to a six-month low of 639.81. However, dealers said the upside was capped as the market remained unconvinced.
"You never know when the government would change its mind and announce something," said a local broker.
City Developments and Wing Tai fell Singapore 50 cents and 12 cents respectively to S$11.50 and S$3.72. Bank stocks like UOB foreign bounced from a new year low to end unchanged at S$13.40.
Malaysia's KLI Holdings, which also ended unchanged at S$1.81, was the most active with about seven million traded. Dealers said there was forced selling on the counter.
Singapore Telecom touched an all time low of S$2.35 in active trading before ending at S$2.37, down one cent.
